chapter: Thomas, own bands and neighborhood clubs
title: Other neighborhood clubs: River Bell, Mama Lou's, Lodgett's, Manny's
summary: Barnes lists the clubs he worked after the Home Inn, with Lawrence on trumpet, and playing trombone at Manny's.

people.name: Lawrence (trumpet player in Barnes's small-club bands)

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Like, other neighborhood places? I worked at the River Bell, out here on, on, on, Crue and Chord, I believe, on that side of the band. That was before you went to the Hominé Inn? No after.

I left the Hominé, because he told us to go out there and try to build a place. I went out there, to try to build a place, and the police was going fine. Mm-hm. And the cops started coming around, and the people got scared, man. How about the- I went back to the club, then we left from there, went back to Tulane there, and, yeah. Back to Tulane there, caught, and there, but on this side of the band, right across the ball club. See, Harry was running there. I was waiting there for him a long time. Who? Harry. He was waiting there. He was running the place there.
How about this place, Mama Lou's? Did you ever play there?
We worked out at Mama Lou's just about three or four years ago. A little before. But I wasn't working out of my job. I worked out there with Andrew Drippchen. And he's job. How about, excuse me,
Oh, I opened Lodgett's. You opened that up.

Who was the trumpet player then? Lawrence. Lawrence. Yeah. Lawrence. Yeah. That must have been a long time ago. It was quite a while, in both places. And the Lurch is over in the Humming Inn. Yes, the old Humming Inn. Because I worked for Lurchin, a long time, small, long, and many years old in Hymn. Because the day that comes to the Lurchin, I'm a little bit of a little bit of a little bit of an arrangement to build their own business business business business business business business business business business business business business business business business business business business business business business business business business business business business business business business business business business business business
Your favorite trumpet player at this time was Ronas? Yeah. He played most of these little clubs with you, didn't he? All of them.
All of them. And then? Just later I stopped playing, and he quit too.
And Manny's Tavern too, Benefit and St. Rocky, I heard you.
Oh, yeah. Well, I played out there with Dylan and the B. Today. Yeah. I had a trombone.
Did you ever have a trombone on these little trombones? No.
Never used that. Mostly short. Well, at Manny's. At Manny's. Oh, at Manny's, yeah. Because I played trombone now with him. Yeah, at Harrison's playing trombone.
